rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone does something angrily.

example.english: They furiously scolded me, saying I shouldn't have done that.
example.traditional: 佢嬲住鬧我，話我唔應該咁做。
example.jyutping: keoi5 nau1 zyu6 naau6 ngo5 waa6 ngo5 m4 jing1 goi1 gam3 zou6

rows.note: Use this when someone acts frantically or puts in extreme effort to get something done.

example.english: I furiously pedaled my bike and finally got to work on time.
example.traditional: 我搏命咁踩單車，終於趕得切返工。
example.jyutping: ngo5 bok3 meng6 gam3 caai2 daan1 ce1 zung1 jyu1 gon2 dak1 cit3 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this for visibly intense embarrassment or agitation, especially when someone is flushed and red-faced.

example.english: They furiously argued with someone, their whole face turning red.
example.traditional: 佢面紅耳赤咁同人爭論，成塊面都紅晒。
example.jyutping: keoi5 min6 hung4 ji5 cek3 gam3 tung4 jan4 zang1 leon6 seng4 faai3 min6 dou1 hung4 saai3
